passage:
In the nurse's office, there was a blue chair beside the window. Students sat there when they had headaches, stomachaches, or simply needed a quiet moment.
One day, the chair broke. The nurse planned to throw it away. But students asked her not to.
They wrote notes about the chair. One said, "I sat here when I cried after a fight." Another said, "This chair helped me calm down before my speech."
The nurse was surprised. To her, it was just old furniture. To students, it was a safe place.
The school repaired the chair and kept it by the window. Sometimes an object becomes important because of the feelings people leave there.
